messages.text: I'm already on SNAP. Is there anything else I might be eligible for? I'm pregnant.

Congratulations! Yes, you may be able to get more help. Pregnant women can often qualify for WIC (food and nutrition help) and TennCare or CoverKids (health coverage). I'll need a few details to check.

1. Who lives with you and shares food? Please give everyone's age.
2. How many babies are you expecting?

After that, I'll ask about income before taxes.
Just me, I live alone. I'm 22. Only one baby.

Thanks! Now a couple of questions about money.

1. Do you have any income before taxes, like a job, unemployment, or Social Security? If so, how much, and how often are you paid (weekly, every two weeks, or monthly)?
2. Are you a U.S. citizen? You can skip this one if you'd rather not say.
I earn $1,400 a month before taxes. I get paid once a month. And yes, I'm a U.S. citizen.

Good news: you look likely to qualify for two more programs.

**1. WIC (food and nutrition help): likely**
- WIC serves pregnant women. Because you already get food assistance (SNAP), you automatically meet WIC's income test.
- WIC also does a short health and nutrition check at the clinic.
- To apply, go to a local health department clinic or call 1-800-DIAL-WIC (1-800-342-5942). Source: [Tennessee Department of Health, WIC](https://www.tn.gov/health/wic.html).
- The rules are in [7 CFR 246.7](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-7/section-246.7) and [7 CFR 246.2](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-7/section-246.2).

**2. TennCare (health coverage): likely**
- Pregnant women can get TennCare with income up to 250% of the poverty level. For you, counted as yourself plus one baby (a household of 2), that limit is $4,509 a month. Your income before taxes is $1,400 a month, which is well under it.
- This screening uses your income before taxes. TennCare uses a tax-based income figure, so the real number may differ a little.
- To apply, go to [TennCare Connect](https://tenncareconnect.tn.gov/) or call 855-259-0701.
- Sources: the Division of TennCare's [Eligibility Reference Guide](https://www.tn.gov/coverkids/coverkids/redirect-income-guidelines.html) and [42 CFR 435.603](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/section-435.603).
- Babies born to women on TennCare are covered for their first year, according to the same guide.

**SNAP:** You already get it, so I didn't check it again. If your rent or bills change, tell your SNAP office. Your benefit may change once the baby comes.

For free local help with applying, you can dial **211**.

This is a screening, not a decision. Only the state agency decides who qualifies, and you can apply either way.
